articles.title: Bitcoin Climbs Back Toward $82,000 in Asian Trading as Yen Rally Fades
articles.excerpt: Bitcoin recovered from an overnight dip below $81,000 as Asian stocks and gold bounced, though ETF outflows and $100 oil remain headwinds.
articles.body_md:
Bitcoin found its footing early Friday in Asia after Thursday's slide.

**Where prices stand**

Bitcoin climbed back to nearly $82,000 after trading below $81,000 overnight, CoinDesk reported at 11:13 p.m. ET Thursday. At that point it was testing its 50-day simple moving average, a common gauge of short-term momentum. Ether, XRP, solana and dogecoin moved in a similar pattern.

**What changed overnight**

The early mood in Asia was cautious. The Japanese yen strengthened to 156.07 per dollar, its strongest level since Sept. 18, after hotter-than-expected Japanese inflation data added to expectations of more Bank of Japan rate hikes. A stronger yen can pressure risk assets because the currency is widely borrowed to fund trades elsewhere.

That move did not last. The yen slipped back toward 157, and Japan's Nikkei, South Korea's Kospi and Nasdaq futures recovered from their session lows. Gold also bounced to about $4,020 an ounce from an early low of $3,986, according to CoinDesk.

**The headwinds**

About $435 million in crypto futures positions were liquidated over 24 hours, including $385 million in bullish bets, a sign that leverage had leaned toward buyers. U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs saw $381 million in outflows Thursday, according to preliminary SoSoValue data cited by CoinDesk, a reversal after more than $1 billion of inflows earlier in the week.

**Why it matters for crypto**

Oil remains a key variable. WTI crude was trading near $100 even after a new White House push to raise U.S. fuel output. Persistent energy-driven inflation could keep interest rates higher, which tends to weigh on bitcoin and other risk assets.
articles.author: Blackmint Desk

articles.title: Solana's Alpenglow Upgrade Goes Live, Cutting Finality to About 150 Milliseconds
articles.excerpt: Solana replaced its original consensus system on mainnet, aiming to make transactions final in about 150 milliseconds instead of roughly 12.8 seconds.
articles.body_md:
Solana has completed the largest change to its core protocol since the network launched in 2020.

**What happened**

The Alpenglow consensus upgrade activated on mainnet at the start of epoch 1064 on Wednesday, Oct. 21, according to the Solana Foundation. Validators kept running the old system, TowerBFT, for about 5,000 slots before the new protocol took over at slot 459,653,000. The Solana Foundation said the handoff took about 900 milliseconds, with 446 of 654 participating validators voting to certify the starting block.

Anza, the engineering firm that built Alpenglow, said finality, the point at which a transaction can no longer be reversed, drops from about 12.8 seconds to roughly 150 milliseconds. CoinDesk noted that 150 milliseconds is a target under normal network conditions rather than a guarantee for every payment.

**How it works**

Under the old design, validators voted by sending transactions on the chain. With Alpenglow's voting protocol, called Votor, they send votes directly to one another and bundle them into certificates, so a block can be final after one or two voting rounds. A second piece, Rotor, which will change how block data spreads across the network, is planned but not yet scheduled.

**What users notice**

Wallets, apps and fees stay the same. CoinDesk pointed out one side effect: because validator votes are no longer recorded as transactions, dashboards that counted them will show lower transaction totals even if real user activity is unchanged.

**Why it matters for crypto**

Faster, near-instant settlement is aimed at exchanges, merchants and financial firms that wait for finality before treating money as moved. CoinDesk reported SOL fell 2.4% to around $104 on Thursday morning amid a broad market dip, so the upgrade has not yet shown up in price.
articles.author: Blackmint Desk

articles.title: a16z Renames Its Crypto Arm 'a16z Frontier' and Widens Its Focus to AI and Robotics
articles.excerpt: Andreessen Horowitz is renaming a16z Crypto to a16z Frontier, adding AI and robotics while saying it will keep investing in crypto.
articles.body_md:
One of crypto's best-known venture investors is changing its name and broadening its scope.

**What happened**

Andreessen Horowitz said Thursday it is renaming a16z Crypto to a16z Frontier. In a blog post, managing partner Chris Dixon said the new fund will back "frontier" startups building technologies and markets that may take years to develop, including artificial intelligence, robotics and new kinds of networks.

Dixon stressed that the firm is not walking away from digital assets. "This is an expansion: we will continue to invest in crypto and related ventures and advocate for sensible crypto regulation," he wrote.

He argued that as blockchains are used more widely, the label matters less. Wall Street and fintech firms now regularly launch products built on blockchains, he said, so it makes more sense to define companies by what they do than by the technology underneath.

**Who is involved**

Dixon will lead the fund with a16z founders Marc Andreessen and Ben Horowitz and general partners Eddy Lazzarin and Guy Wuollet. Fortune reported that the change widens the scope of a $2.2 billion fund announced in May. TechCrunch reported the unit has raised nearly $10 billion across five funds since 2018, with past bets including Coinbase.

**Why it matters for crypto**

The move can be read two ways. TechCrunch framed it as a sign that crypto-only investing has lost some of its pull with venture firms. Dixon's own framing is that blockchain technology is becoming ordinary infrastructure inside wider tech. Either way, the shift suggests crypto startups may increasingly compete with AI and other emerging fields for the same pool of venture money.
articles.author: Blackmint Desk

articles.title: Chainlink Teams Up With LG CNS to Build Out Korea's Digital Asset Infrastructure
articles.excerpt: LG Group's tech arm will add Chainlink's cross-chain and data tools to its digital asset platforms and work on expanding Korean won stablecoins.
articles.body_md:
Chainlink has landed a partnership with one of South Korea's largest corporate groups.

**What happened**

Chainlink announced a strategic partnership with LG CNS, the IT services and AI arm of LG Group, The Block reported Thursday. LG CNS will build Chainlink's cross-chain, data and orchestration tools into the digital asset platforms it offers to Korean institutions.

The two companies also said they will work on expanding the use and distribution of Korean stablecoins, a segment The Block described as having more than 11 million eligible users, and on helping develop the country's digital asset framework.

"Korea's financial infrastructure is entering the tokenization era," said Hongkeun Kim, executive vice president and head of the digital business division at LG CNS, according to the announcement. He said the partnership aims to speed up the growth of Korea's tokenized securities market.

**The backdrop**

South Korea does not yet have a clear legal basis for issuing and trading stablecoins tied to the won. Lawmakers and the government are working on the Digital Asset Basic Act, which would set rules for won stablecoins and other parts of the market, according to The Block.

LG CNS is also the lead contractor for the Bank of Korea's digital currency effort, Project Hangang. The announcement did not say Chainlink would be part of that project.

**Why it matters for crypto**

Korea is one of the world's most active crypto markets, which The Block put at about $68 billion. A tie-up with a major conglomerate's tech arm gives Chainlink a foothold with Korean institutions as the country moves toward formal rules for stablecoins and tokenized assets. The Block's market ticker showed LINK near $12.12 late Thursday.
articles.author: Blackmint Desk

articles.title: Ripple and Arf Bring RLUSD Settlement Financing to the XRP Ledger
articles.excerpt: Swiss payments-finance firm Arf will offer short-term RLUSD working capital to licensed payment companies on the XRP Ledger.
articles.body_md:
Ripple's dollar stablecoin is getting a new job in cross-border payments.

**What happened**

Ripple and Arf, a Swiss payments-finance firm based in Zug, announced a partnership on Oct. 22 to provide settlement liquidity in RLUSD on the XRP Ledger, crypto.news reported. Arf will lend short-term working capital to licensed payment companies, such as remittance and card businesses, that need money in place while international transfers clear.

Arf's loans typically run one to five days. As each payment settles, the borrower repays, and the capital can be lent out again. Arf co-founder and CEO Ali Erhat Nalbant said the firm handles about $10 billion in annual settlement volume, with its capital turning over four times a month.

"Through this partnership with Ripple, we're bringing stablecoin working capital to the XRP Ledger," Nalbant said.

**What's not settled yet**

The announcement did not say how much RLUSD will be committed or how much volume will move through the ledger at first. A later phase depends on two proposed XRP Ledger features, Single Asset Vaults and a native Lending Protocol, which still need validator approval before going live. Under the plan, RLUSD would fund the loans while XRP would cover network fees and reserves. The announcement did not require payment firms to buy XRP.

**Why it matters for crypto**

Payment companies often tie up large sums pre-funding accounts in different countries. Short-term stablecoin credit is one way blockchains are being pitched as practical plumbing for that business, and the deal adds a real-world use case for RLUSD as stablecoin rules take shape in the U.S.
articles.author: Blackmint Desk

articles.title: Robinhood Chain Passes $1.1 Billion in Locked Value as Stock Tokens Become Loan Collateral
articles.excerpt: Eligible holders can now borrow stablecoins against Robinhood Stock Tokens on Morpho, as DefiLlama data put Robinhood Chain's DeFi TVL at $1.14 billion.
articles.body_md:
Robinhood's blockchain is adding a new way for users outside the U.S. to put tokenized stocks to work.

**What happened**

Robinhood Crypto said on Oct. 22 that its Stock Tokens can now be used as collateral on Morpho, a decentralized lending protocol, allowing eligible holders to borrow stablecoins against them, crypto.news reported. "Robinhood Chain brings the rails, Morpho brings their credit layer," the company wrote.

Morpho's dashboard listed markets such as NVDA/USDG, GOOGL/USDG and AAPL/USDG, each with a 62.5% liquidation threshold. That means a loan can be liquidated if the debt grows past that share of the collateral's value, for example after a drop in the stock price.

**The numbers**

DefiLlama's Oct. 22 data put Robinhood Chain's total value locked in DeFi at $1.14 billion, with about $1.08 billion in stablecoins on the network, according to crypto.news. Decentralized exchanges on the chain handled about $6.1 billion over seven days. Morpho separately showed about $1.10 billion in deposits and $484.3 million in outstanding loans across all collateral types on the chain.

**Important limits**

Robinhood's disclosures say Stock Tokens are not registered under U.S. securities laws and cannot be offered to U.S. persons, with further restrictions in Canada, the U.K. and Switzerland. The tokens give economic exposure to shares but no legal rights in the underlying company. Stock price feeds also update only five days a week, which borrowers should keep in mind.

**Why it matters for crypto**

Robinhood Chain launched its public mainnet on July 1 on Arbitrum technology. Passing $1 billion in locked value within about four months shows growing activity around tokenized real-world assets, one of the sector's main growth themes this year.
articles.author: Blackmint Desk

articles.title: Jobless Claims Fall to 194,000, Near Lowest Since 1969, as Fed Meeting Nears
articles.excerpt: First-time U.S. unemployment claims dropped to 194,000, reinforcing a steady labor market as markets expect the Fed to hold next week.
articles.body_md:
Layoffs in the U.S. remain rare, giving the Federal Reserve one less reason to worry about jobs as it weighs inflation.

**The data**

Initial claims for unemployment benefits fell to a seasonally adjusted 194,000 for the week ended Oct. 17, the Labor Department said Thursday, CNBC reported. That is just above the 189,000 recorded in mid-July, the lowest since September 1969. The four-week average dipped to 197,750, and claims have averaged 212,000 over the past year.

Hiring, though, is soft. Payrolls grew by only 29,000 in September and have averaged about 69,000 a month this year, while the unemployment rate rose to 4.2%. Economists describe this as a "low-hire, low-fire" job market.

"The claims data suggests that labor market conditions are stable," Thomas Simons, chief U.S. economist at Jefferies, said in a client note quoted by CNBC.

**The Fed angle**

Fed officials meet next week. CNBC reported that policymakers have described the labor market as a source of strength and are focused more on inflation, which remains well above the 2% target. Markets expect the Fed to hold rates in October and then raise them by a quarter point in December, according to CNBC. The October jobs report is due Nov. 6.

**Why it matters for crypto**

A steady job market keeps the Fed's attention on inflation, and with oil prices high, that leans toward tighter policy. Higher rates raise the appeal of cash and bonds relative to non-yielding assets like bitcoin. Crypto traders will be watching next week's decision and the Fed's tone for hints about December.
articles.author: Blackmint Desk

articles.title: Trump Invokes Defense Production Act to Boost U.S. Oil and Fuel Output
articles.excerpt: A presidential memo declares petroleum production and refining essential to national defense, opening the door to federal support as oil hovers near $100.
articles.body_md:
The White House is using a Cold War-era law to try to ease high fuel prices.

**What happened**

President Donald Trump on Thursday determined that petroleum production, refining and related activities are essential to national defense, CNBC reported. The presidential memo invokes part of the Defense Production Act, allowing the government to offer financial incentives for oil-related activity, pipelines and fuel storage.

The memo said that without such action, the U.S. could not provide enough of those energy services in a "timely manner due to constrained financing, long lead times, permitting and infrastructure bottlenecks, and supply chain limitations." It did not name specific projects. Last week, Vice President JD Vance said the administration would use the law to expand a Texas refinery owned by Delek U.S. Holdings, according to CNBC.

**The backdrop**

Crude and diesel prices have surged since the U.S. and Israel attacked Iran at the end of February, limiting energy shipments worldwide, CNBC reported, with Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries adding to shortages. High fuel costs are a political issue ahead of the Nov. 3 elections.

**Why it matters for crypto**

Oil has become one of the main forces behind interest-rate expectations. CoinDesk reported that WTI crude was still trading near $100 early Friday in Asia, and that the order had yet to materially cool prices. Building refining capacity takes time, so the move may do little in the near term. As long as energy keeps inflation elevated, central banks are less likely to ease, a backdrop that has weighed on bitcoin and other risk assets this month.
articles.author: Blackmint Desk

articles.title: Japan's Core Inflation Tops 2% Target, Strengthening Case for Another BOJ Hike
articles.excerpt: Japan's core CPI rose 2.1% in September, above the Bank of Japan's goal for the first time in nine months, as analysts eye a December hike.
articles.body_md:
Price pressures in Japan are broadening, and that matters for global markets, crypto included.

**The data**

Japan's core consumer price index, which excludes fresh food, rose 2.1% in September from a year earlier, data showed Friday, according to Reuters reporting carried by CNA. That matched forecasts, sped up from 1.7% in August, and topped the Bank of Japan's 2% target for the first time in nine months. A narrower measure that also strips out fuel, watched closely by the BOJ, rose 2.4%, up from 1.9%.

Higher fuel costs tied to the Middle East conflict, a weak yen that raises import prices, and demand linked to AI all fed into the numbers.

**What the BOJ may do**

The BOJ raised its policy rate to 1.25%, a 31-year high, last month. Sources told Reuters it is likely to hold at its meeting ending Oct. 30 but may raise its inflation forecast. Many analysts polled by Reuters expect a move to 1.50% in December. "With little evidence that the tightening delivered so far has slowed the economy, the risks are shifting towards a higher peak in the policy rate," said Marcel Thieliant of Capital Economics.

**Why it matters for crypto**

The yen is widely borrowed to fund investments elsewhere, so expectations of higher Japanese rates can prompt investors to unwind those trades and sell risk assets. CoinDesk reported the yen briefly jumped to 156.07 per dollar after the data before slipping back toward 157, while bitcoin dipped below $81,000 and then recovered toward $82,000. Further BOJ hikes are a risk crypto traders will keep watching.
articles.author: Blackmint Desk

articles.title: Central Banks Split Three Ways as Energy-Driven Inflation Lingers
articles.excerpt: The Philippines delivered a surprise half-point hike, South Korea held at 3% and Turkey trimmed rates, as high energy prices push central banks in different directions.
articles.body_md:
Three central banks in Asia and Europe announced rate decisions on Thursday, and they went three different ways, a sign of how unevenly high energy prices are hitting economies.

**Philippines: a bigger hike than expected**

The Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas raised its key rate by 50 basis points to 5.50%, its fourth increase in a row, Reuters reported. All 27 economists in a Reuters poll had expected a smaller, quarter-point move. Inflation in the Philippines jumped to 7.2% in September from 6.1% in August, driven by rice, electricity, fuel and transport costs. The peso firmed to 63.311 per U.S. dollar after the announcement, according to Reuters.

**South Korea: a pause after two hikes**

The Bank of Korea left its base rate at 3.00% in a unanimous vote. Its statement cited strong export-led growth and inflation near 3%, but said the Middle East conflict and policy in major economies had made the outlook more uncertain. The board said it will decide "the timing and pace of further increases in the Base Rate" based on inflation, growth and financial stability.

**Turkey: another small cut**

Turkey's central bank cut its one-week repo rate to 36% from 37%, saying the underlying trend of inflation is slowing. It warned that elevated energy prices tied to geopolitical tensions remain an upside risk and that policy "will be tightened" if the inflation outlook worsens significantly and persistently.

**Why it matters for crypto**

Oil-driven inflation is the common thread, and it is the same pressure facing the Federal Reserve, which meets Oct. 27-28 with another hike still on the table, Decrypt reported. Traders in bitcoin and other risk assets will be watching whether the Fed leans toward the hawkish end of this range.
articles.author: Blackmint Desk

articles.title: Bitcoin Holds Near $81,400 as Wall Street's Tech Selloff Weighs on Crypto
articles.excerpt: Bitcoin finished the U.S. trading day down about 3.6% over 24 hours as the Nasdaq fell 2.6% on renewed doubts about AI spending.
articles.body_md:
Crypto spent Thursday moving in step with a sharp slide in technology stocks.

**Where prices stand**

As U.S. markets closed, bitcoin was at about $81,400, down 3.6% over 24 hours, CoinDesk reported at 4:08 p.m. ET. That was roughly $600 above its low of the session. Earlier, at 2:01 p.m. ET, CoinDesk had bitcoin near its low at about $81,100, with ether and XRP each down more than 5%.

**What drove it**

The pressure started overnight. CoinDesk reported that mixed quarterly results from Tesla and Meta revived doubts about how much big companies are spending on artificial intelligence, pulling down stocks in Asia before the U.S. open. Altcoins fell harder than bitcoin, and a CoinDesk index of decentralized-finance tokens dropped 5.6% in the morning.

By the close, the Nasdaq had lost 2.6% and the S&P 500 1.2%, while the Dow ended flat as money moved into defensive sectors like health care and consumer staples. Crypto-linked shares were hit early in the session. CoinDesk reported that shortly after the open, Strategy was down 5.6%, Circle 4.6%, MARA Holdings 4.2% and Coinbase 4%.

**Why it matters for crypto**

Thursday showed again how closely bitcoin can trade with tech stocks when investors pull back from risk. Even so, CoinDesk noted in the morning that options markets were calm, with implied-volatility gauges for bitcoin and ether sitting just above their 2026 lows. Traders will be watching whether that calm holds if the tech selloff continues.
articles.author: Blackmint Desk

articles.title: Treasury Yields Post Biggest Drop Since 2023 as Fed Hike Bets Fade and Oil Jumps
articles.excerpt: The 10-year yield fell below 5% for the first time since Sept. 23 as investors fled stocks, even as Brent crude rose 4% on a report about possible strikes on Iran.
articles.body_md:
Investors rushed into U.S. government bonds on Thursday, sending borrowing costs sharply lower even as oil prices climbed.

**A big day for bonds**

The 10-year Treasury yield fell more than 17 basis points to 4.972%, CNBC reported. It was the first time the yield had dipped below 5% since Sept. 23, and the largest one-day drop since March 10, 2023. The 2-year yield, which tracks expectations for Fed policy, fell more than 16 basis points to 4.659%.

"For the first time in a while, Treasurys are enjoying haven status," Larry Holzenthaler of Catalyst Funds told CNBC.

**Fed hike odds shrink**

CoinDesk reported at 2:01 p.m. ET that the odds of a Fed rate hike at next week's meeting were close to zero, and that the odds of no further hikes this year had risen to 28% from 10%.

**Oil moves the other way**

Brent crude rose 4% to $113.17 a barrel and U.S. crude closed at $99.47, CNBC reported. The gains followed a New York Times report, citing unnamed U.S. officials, that the U.S. and Israel are considering a "short but intensive" round of strikes on Iran after the Nov. 3 midterm elections. CoinDesk noted that rates and oil, which moved closely together for months, have recently split apart.

**Why it matters for crypto**

Lower yields can make assets like bitcoin, which pay no interest, look more attractive. On Thursday, though, crypto traded with tech stocks and fell. Gregory Faranello of South Street Securities told CNBC that if energy prices "stay elevated, it could force the Fed's hand to do even more." That leaves oil as a key risk for crypto ahead of the Fed's decision.
articles.author: Blackmint Desk

articles.title: Banks and Crypto Firms Split Over OCC's Final Stablecoin Rule
articles.excerpt: The OCC became the first regulator to finalize GENIUS Act rules. Banks say it leaves room for stablecoin yield, while crypto groups say it follows the law.
articles.body_md:
The first final rule under the GENIUS Act, the U.S. stablecoin law, has reopened an old fight between banks and the crypto industry.

**What the OCC decided**

The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency announced the rule on Wednesday. It sets standards for stablecoin issuers under its oversight, including foreign issuers, covering reserve backing, redemption, risk management and certain custody activities. Anti-money-laundering and sanctions rules will come in a separate rulemaking with the Treasury. The rule and the law take effect Jan. 18, 2027. Comptroller Jonathan V. Gould called it "a clear, practical framework for payment stablecoin innovation."

The Block reported that the OCC is the first U.S. regulator to finalize rules under the act. Issuers are still barred from paying interest directly to holders. But the OCC dropped a proposed presumption that some reward arrangements with third parties, such as trading platforms, could be unlawful. It will review those case by case instead.

**The reaction**

American Bankers Association CEO Rob Nichols said the rule "will preserve the status quo for crypto platforms despite Congress's clear intent to protect local lending." The Blockchain Association's Lindsay Fraser said dropping the presumption "brings the final rule more closely in line with the statutory text," The Block reported.

Analysts at TD Cowen, in a note quoted by The Block, said: "Until the courts rule, there will be ambiguity on what is permitted and what is prohibited, which is a negative."

**Why it matters for crypto**

Rewards on stablecoin balances are a draw for exchanges and their users. The ruling keeps that option open for now, but other regulators still have rules to finish, and the same question was a sticking point in talks on the broader Clarity Act, which has yet to advance in the Senate.
articles.author: Blackmint Desk

articles.title: Ireland's Central Bank Fines Coinbase Unit €3.25 Million Over Customer-Fund Safeguards
articles.excerpt: Coinbase Ireland admitted it failed to properly protect customer funds between 2020 and 2025. The fine still needs High Court approval.
articles.body_md:
Ireland's financial regulator has fined Coinbase's Irish e-money business over how it protected customer money.

**The penalty**

The Central Bank of Ireland said on Thursday that it fined Coinbase Ireland Limited €3,252,618 (about $3.6 million, per CoinDesk and The Block) for breaking safeguarding and outsourcing rules between Nov. 1, 2020, and Aug. 19, 2025. The penalty started at €4,646,597 and was cut by 30% under a settlement. Coinbase Ireland admitted the breaches and accepted a reprimand. The sanctions take effect only once the High Court confirms them.

**What went wrong**

The regulator said the unit leaned too heavily on its U.S. parent to run its safeguarding controls and lacked enough local expertise to oversee them. It also said the dedicated account meant to hold customer funds was underfunded for long stretches. According to the settlement notice, as reported by The Block, daily shortfalls reached €5.2 million in 2024. About 30 institutional clients also paid dollars into accounts held by Coinbase Inc. rather than the Irish entity between March 2023 and October 2024.

Coinbase said the issues are fully resolved and no customers lost money or were unable to reach their funds, The Block reported. The company said it reported several of the problems itself in January 2024. The Block noted this follows a €21.5 million fine on Coinbase Europe in November 2025 over transaction monitoring.

**Why it matters for crypto**

Keeping customer money separate and fully backed is one of the basic protections regulators expect from exchanges. This case shows Ireland's regulator holding one of the world's largest trading platforms to those standards.
articles.author: Blackmint Desk

articles.title: Bitcoin's Overnight Round Trip to $85,000 Ends Below $82,000
articles.excerpt: Bitcoin neared $85,000 late Wednesday, then fell under $82,000 Thursday morning as oil jumped and tech stocks slid, leaving about $431 million in liquidations.
articles.body_md:
Bitcoin gave back its midweek bounce in a matter of hours. The largest cryptocurrency pushed close to $85,000 late Wednesday, then slid to roughly $81,800 by early Thursday, a swing of about $3,000 in less than a day.

**Where prices stood**

Yahoo Finance reported bitcoin opened Thursday at $84,024.44 and had fallen to $81,809.90 by 7:15 a.m. ET. Ether dropped from an open of $2,471.35 to $2,400.36 over the same window. CoinDesk had bitcoin at $81,650 at 8:15 a.m. ET.

**Traders caught on both sides**

Citing CoinGlass data, CoinDesk said about $431 million in leveraged positions were forcibly closed over 24 hours. Roughly $173 million of that hit short sellers on the way up. On the way down, bullish bets took most of the damage. A liquidation happens when an exchange closes a borrowed-money position because the trader can no longer cover losses.

**Why the mood turned**

The slide lined up with a broader retreat from risk. Brent crude topped $112 a barrel on new attacks in the Gulf region, South Korea's Kospi fell about 3.5%, and U.S. tech futures dropped after weak outlooks from Tesla and Lam Research, according to CoinDesk and Yahoo Finance. Yahoo noted that higher oil feeds inflation worries, which tends to make speculative assets less attractive.

**What to watch**

CoinDesk said some market watchers view $82,500 as a key level for bitcoin. Before this week, bitcoin had dipped under $80,000 during a mid-October slide, so traders are watching whether the latest pullback holds above that zone.
articles.author: Blackmint Desk

articles.title: Oil Hits Five-Month High on Gulf Attacks as Fed Hike Bets Fade
articles.excerpt: Brent crude reached $112.55 on Houthi strikes in Saudi Arabia, while a rush into Treasuries pulled yields lower and cut the odds of a Fed rate hike next week.
articles.body_md:
Two big forces are pulling on markets at once: an oil shock from the Middle East and shifting bets on the Federal Reserve.

**Oil climbs on new attacks**

Brent crude touched $112.55 a barrel on Thursday, its highest since May 18, Reuters reported. Prices jumped after Yemen's Houthis struck several targets in Saudi Arabia on Wednesday, including a civilian airport in Dammam and an oil field. Reuters also reported that Saudi Aramco told staff to leave its Dhahran headquarters and work remotely, citing six people familiar with the matter.

"No de-escalation is anticipated until the US midterm elections, which should keep oil prices elevated," PVM Oil analyst Tamas Varga told Reuters.

**Rate-hike odds shrink**

With oil and inflation running hot, the Fed has been leaning toward tighter policy. But a selloff in AI-linked stocks sent investors into U.S. government bonds. CoinDesk reported the 10-year Treasury yield fell to about 5.02%, and CME FedWatch put the odds of a hike at next week's Fed meeting at 8% as of 10:25 a.m. ET, down from 28% a week earlier.

**Why it matters for crypto**

Expensive oil can keep inflation sticky, which makes it harder for the Fed to ease. That has tended to weigh on bitcoin and other risk assets, and both stocks and crypto fell Thursday morning. Lower bond yields could ease some of that pressure. The Fed's next decision is due on Oct. 28, and traders will watch it, along with oil, to judge where crypto goes next.
articles.author: Blackmint Desk

articles.title: China Moves to Confiscate 61,800 Bitcoin Seized in Britain
articles.excerpt: A court in Tianjin has accepted a bid to confiscate more than 61,800 BTC tied to a $5.7 billion fraud, opening a second legal fight over coins held by U.K. authorities.
articles.body_md:
Chinese prosecutors are seeking to confiscate more than 61,800 bitcoin connected to one of the country's largest alleged investment frauds. The coins are currently held by authorities in the United Kingdom.

**The case**

According to CoinDesk and crypto.news, citing Chinese media, the Tianjin No. 2 Intermediate People's Court said on Oct. 13 that it had accepted the prosecutors' application on Sept. 28. The case centers on Qian Zhimin, whose company allegedly sold unlicensed investment products between 2014 and 2017. Prosecutors say it raised about 40.4 billion yuan (roughly $5.7 billion) from more than 102,000 investors, who lost close to 20 billion yuan.

Qian left China in 2017 and was later convicted and jailed in the U.K. British police seized the bitcoin, along with other crypto and assets. The court has given victims and other interested parties six months to join the proceedings.

**Two countries, one stash**

The Chinese move follows a recent ruling by the U.K. High Court that Chinese law should govern victims' ownership claims to the coins. CoinDesk reported that the ruling does not settle who ultimately receives the bitcoin, and further hearings are expected. Unchained, via Yahoo Finance, valued the 61,896 coins at about $5.1 billion at a bitcoin price near $82,200, based on CoinGecko data.

**Why it matters**

This is one of the largest single government-held bitcoin stashes. Traders watch such holdings closely because a decision to sell them could add supply to the market. No sale has been announced.
articles.author: Blackmint Desk

articles.title: Drift Hacker Pushes Over $100 Million in Ether Through Tornado Cash
articles.excerpt: Wallets tied to April's Drift Protocol exploit sent an estimated $109 million to $122 million in ETH into Tornado Cash on Oct. 20-21, trackers say.
articles.body_md:
Funds stolen in one of this year's largest crypto hacks are on the move again.

**What happened**

Wallets linked to the April 1 exploit of Drift Protocol, a Solana-based trading platform, deposited a large amount of ether into the mixing service Tornado Cash on Oct. 20 and 21, blockchain trackers report. Estimates differ. Arkham Intelligence put the total at about $122.3 million across 520 deposits, according to CoinDesk, calling it the largest round of hacker-linked Tornado Cash deposits in two years. Onchain Lens counted about 44,510 ETH, or roughly $109 million, according to crypto.news, while Lookonchain tracked about 25,700 ETH on the first day alone.

Tornado Cash pools deposits and pays them out to new addresses, which makes stolen funds much harder to trace. A deposit there does not mean the funds have been turned into cash.

**Background**

Drift lost about $295 million in the attack, according to crypto.news. Drift has attributed the hack to a North Korean group following an investigation by security firm Mandiant, and it opened recovery claims for affected users on Oct. 1. Arkham data cited by crypto.news showed the exploiter's tracked wallets still held about 56,569 ETH after Wednesday's transfers.

**Why it matters**

Large movements of stolen funds can put pressure on prices if the coins are later sold, and they renew scrutiny of DeFi security and crypto privacy tools. For Drift users, the transfers lower the odds that the mixed funds will be recovered.

articles.title: Bitcoin Gives Back Overnight Gains, Slipping Below $82,000
articles.excerpt: Bitcoin climbed to nearly $85,000 late Wednesday, then dropped back by Thursday morning. That move hit traders who had bet in both directions.
articles.body_md:
Bitcoin climbed to nearly $85,000 late Wednesday, then dropped back by Thursday morning. That move hit traders who had bet in both directions.

Yahoo Finance reported that bitcoin opened Thursday at $84,024.44. By 7:15 a.m. ET it had fallen to $81,809.90. CoinDesk put it at $81,650 as of 8:15 a.m. EDT. Ether was also lower. Yahoo listed it at $2,400.36 at 7:15 a.m. ET.

CoinDesk cited CoinGlass data showing about $431 million in leveraged positions were forcibly closed over 24 hours. Liquidations like these happen when traders using borrowed money can't cover their losses. Roughly $173 million of the total came from short sellers during the climb. Most of the losses after that fell on traders betting on higher prices.

Wider markets were also uneasy. Brent crude oil traded above $111 a barrel after renewed hostilities in the Middle East, Yahoo Finance reported. U.S. stock futures fell after weak outlooks from Tesla and Lam Research. CoinDesk noted that some market watchers see $82,500 as an important level for bitcoin.

The pullback came one day after bitcoin bounced back from a mid-October slide that had briefly taken it below $80,000.

articles.title: U.S. Bank Regulator Finalizes First Stablecoin Rule Under GENIUS Act
articles.excerpt: The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) issued a final rule on Wednesday putting the GENIUS Act into practice. The GENIUS Act is the federal law that governs dollar-backed "payment stablecoins."
articles.body_md:
The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) issued a final rule on Wednesday putting the GENIUS Act into practice. The GENIUS Act is the federal law that governs dollar-backed "payment stablecoins."

The rule sets requirements for stablecoin issuers under the OCC's oversight, including foreign issuers and certain custody activities. It covers how reserves must back the coins, how holders can redeem them and how risk must be managed. Anti-money-laundering and sanctions rules will come later in a separate rulemaking with the Treasury Department. Both the rule and the law take effect on Jan. 18, 2027.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent called the GENIUS Act "a watershed moment in American finance." Comptroller Jonathan V. Gould said the rule provides "a clear, practical framework for payment stablecoin innovation."

CoinDesk reported that a closely watched question is still open. The law bans issuers from paying yield solely for holding a stablecoin. The OCC said it will judge rewards programs case by case, and existing programs on exchanges won't get special protection. The OCC is the first federal agency to finalize its rules under the act. Other regulators are still working on theirs.

articles.title: Solana Switches On Alpenglow, Its Biggest Network Change in Years
articles.excerpt: Solana's main network has moved to a new consensus system called Alpenglow. Consensus is the process validators use to agree that transactions are final.
articles.body_md:
Solana's main network has moved to a new consensus system called Alpenglow. Consensus is the process validators use to agree that transactions are final.

According to the Solana Foundation, Alpenglow went live at the start of epoch 1064 on Wednesday, Oct. 21, at about 13:36 UTC (9:36 a.m. ET). The network kept running its old TowerBFT system for roughly 18 more minutes before handing over. The foundation said 446 of the network's 654 validators signed off on the switch.

The main goal is speed. Under TowerBFT, a transaction took about 12.8 seconds to become final. Alpenglow aims for about 150 milliseconds. The foundation says wallets and apps should keep working as before, and fees and programs are unchanged.

This first phase adds only Alpenglow's new voting system, called Votor. A second part, Rotor, will change how block data spreads across the network. It is planned for a later release and has no date yet. Anza, the developer that built Alpenglow, had already run the upgrade on Solana's test networks in September.
articles.author: Blackmint Desk
